title: Microeconomic Concepts
definition: Microeconomics is the branch of economics that studies the behavior of individual economic agents—such as households, firms, and industries—in decision-making and allocation of limited resources. It analyzes how prices of goods and services are determined through the interplay of individual demand and supply.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for Prelims (Conceptual clarity on demand-supply shifts, market structures, elasticity, and welfare economics) and Mains GS Paper III (Inclusive growth, industrial policy, pricing mechanisms, subsidies, and market failures).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Microeconomic Concepts.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of scarcity and choice
